subject: general
question: What was the main focus of the First Five-Year Plan?

options.text: The establishment of higher education institution
The agricultural development of the country

solution:
The correct answer is __**The agricultural development of the country**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956)** of India primarily focused on the **agricultural sector** to address the food security needs of the country.
 
• It aimed at increasing agricultural production by implementing measures such as land reforms, irrigation projects, and the use of improved seeds and fertilizers.
 
• Major irrigation projects like the Bhakra Nangal Dam and the Hirakud Dam were initiated during this period to boost agricultural productivity.
 
• The plan allocated around 31% of its total budget to the agriculture and irrigation sectors, highlighting the emphasis on rural development and food self-sufficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• These are centralized and integrated national economic programs developed by the Planning Commission of India.
 
• They were inspired by the Soviet model of planning and were used to guide the economic development of the country.
 
• The first five-year plan was **launched in 1951** and aimed to improve living standards through agricultural development, industrialization, and infrastructure expansion.
 
 
 
• **Irrigation Projects**
 
 
• Key projects initiated during the First Five-Year Plan include the Bhakra Nangal Dam, Hirakud Dam, and Damodar Valley Corporation.
 
• These projects were crucial in providing water for irrigation, generating hydroelectric power, and controlling floods.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**
 
 
• Although the Green Revolution officially began in the 1960s, its seeds were sown during the First Five-Year Plan through the promotion of high-yielding varieties of seeds and the use of fertilizers and pesticides.
 
• It led to a significant increase in food grain production in the following decades, especially in states like Punjab and Haryana.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms**
 
 
• Land reforms were a crucial part of the First Five-Year Plan, aimed at redistributing land to the landless and marginal farmers to ensure equitable land ownership.
 
• This included measures like the abolition of the Zamindari system and the introduction of land ceiling acts.
